output.subject: Re: Drive-through at Wexford Commons
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for getting in touch, and for keeping a sense of humour while you did. We appreciate you taking the time to let us know about this.

You told us that the drive-through at our Wexford Commons branch has been marked "temporarily closed" since July, and that the sign still says it will reopen "soon" without giving a date. You asked a fair question: how soon is soon? You also mentioned that for customers with toddlers in car seats, getting everyone out of the car to go inside isn't a small thing. We understand why an open-ended "soon" is frustrating when you're planning your banking around little ones, and we're sorry for the inconvenience this has caused.

We've passed your message to our Branch & Contact Center team, who will look into the status of the Wexford Commons drive-through and what information we can share with you about when it's expected to reopen.

We will respond to you within 10 business days. In the meantime, if there's anything else you'd like to add, please reply to this email.

Thank you again for your patience and for letting us know.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Confirm the current status of the Wexford Commons drive-through and whether a reopening date can be shared.
Decide whether to mention any alternatives (e.g. other nearby drive-throughs) in the final reply; none are referenced in the draft.
The customer's 'I'll sue' remark is explicitly a joke; no legal threat appears intended, but confirm you're comfortable treating it that way.
Consider whether the branch signage should be updated with clearer timing, as the customer's frustration centres on the vague 'soon'.
